title: Personal Checking: when an account becomes dormant and how it is reactivated
content:
## Scope

This policy governs dormancy on a Personal Checking account: what counts as customer-initiated activity, when an inactive account becomes dormant, the dormant account fee, and reactivation. The inactivity period and the dormant account fee are each tier's own published figures.

## What counts as customer-initiated activity

| Counts | Does not count |
|---|---|
| A deposit or debit the owner initiates through a branch, ATM, debit card, paid check, mobile deposit, online transfer, Zelle or wire | Interest credits |
| An ACH debit the owner authorized | Fees and fee refunds |
| | Direct deposits and other ACH credits |

The account's last customer activity date records the posted date of the latest customer-initiated activity.

## Becoming dormant

An active account becomes dormant once the tier's inactivity period, in calendar months, has passed after the last customer-initiated activity. The clock starts from the last customer activity date on the account; count calendar months from that date; the account is due for dormancy when the current date is on or after that date plus the inactivity period in calendar months, falling back to the last day of the month when that day does not exist. The boundary day itself counts as due.

## While dormant

- The tier's dormant account fee is assessed at each statement cycle close, reduced so that it never takes the ledger balance below zero, and not recorded at all when the balance is already zero or below.
- Dormancy never stops interest crediting or the posting of incoming credits.

## Reactivation

A dormant account is reactivated only when the owner's identity has been verified in the current contact and the owner initiates a transaction. The identity of the owner must be verified before a dormant account is reactivated, as shown by the bank's verification record for the customer. The reactivation date becomes the new last customer activity date.

## Worked cases (hypothetical figures chosen only for illustration)

- **Month-end fallback, with an inactivity period of 18 months:** last customer-initiated activity on 2024-08-31. Eighteen calendar months later would be 2026-02-31, which does not exist, so the account is due for dormancy from 2026-02-28.
- **Fee reduced to the balance, with a dormant account fee of 4.00 USD:** the balance at cycle close is 1.75 USD, so the fee is reduced to 1.75 USD and the balance ends at zero. Had the balance been 0.00 or negative, no fee would be recorded.
- **A direct deposit does not keep the account active:** payroll arriving by direct deposit every month is not customer-initiated activity, so it does not move the last customer activity date.

## Points of judgement

- **Wrong reading:** "a dormant account stops earning interest". **Correct basis:** dormancy never stops interest crediting.
- **Wrong reading:** "any contact from the owner reactivates the account". **Correct basis:** reactivation needs the owner's identity verified in the current contact and a transaction the owner initiates.
